mentl/9671091:
wasm.mn's LMakeClosure arm binds a self-recursive closure's own local to
the record before filling captures, guarded on captures_self, and its
comment names this iteration's symptom verbatim: a null fn_ptr, the
parse_int nested-go indirect-call-type-mismatch that trapped m3 in the
lexer. Someone met this before and wrote the guard; the guard is what
fails now.

The defect is two namespaces in one field. LFn carries a single name, and
the emit spends it on two incompatible things: the table-index global,
deliberately qualified through spec_closure_name, and the local binding,
which must match the source-level name the capture reads. captures_self
compares a capture's LLocal name against fn_name with field_name_eq, so
once lower qualifies, "go" against "parse_int_go" answers false, the
early bind is skipped, and the self-capture reads a zero local. Even
firing, local_wat_name(fn_name, RI32) would bind parse_int_go while the
reader reads go.

The stamp, with its incompleteness stated. Traced: one name field read at
two sites with opposite requirements, diverging exactly when the
discriminator starts working. Priced: a representation change, either LFn
carrying binding name and emitted symbol separately or qualification
moving to emit where both consumers sit, touching every LFn construction
and destructure. Writers: lower mints the names; wasm.mn reads them at
the closure emit, the index global, and captures_self. Not enumerated:
the full LFn site set, which is the next iteration's first move and the
reason this one stops at the stamp.

The ultimate form is an identity comparison — "is this capture the
closure being built" is a handle question being answered by comparing two
strings from different naming schemes. Whether the handles in scope are
comparable is unmeasured, and that measurement decides whether the fix is
a representation change or a one-line read.

Eight iterations without a src landing, named plainly: the row work is
blocked behind this, and this is now

parameter of a reachable generic declaration — generalize's Forall is the
graph's own proof, and repr_of floors it to the honest word by design —
so the report re-derived 'free = error' against that proof: fn ident(x)=x
called from main reported four times on a clean program, the runtime
shadow carried 182 false lines on a clean compile, and ~28.5k of the

the consumer owns the refusal, never the read. The arm is now

EUnresolvedType mints in lower/infer are different semantics and stay.

noodles/96d4825:
The last pass took touch-action to none and panned by writing scrollLeft
by hand, to force the pinch to fire. That killed the browser's momentum
scrolling — the timeline stopped dead on release instead of flicking
like Ableton's does. Wrong trade.

Panning goes back to the native inertial scroll (touch-action: pan-x).
The pinch now rides Touch events (e.touches.length === 2) with
preventDefault, so it reliably owns the two-finger gesture without
fighting the scroll, and still scales the DOM with a transform that
commits real layout once on release. Taps read one pointer and only fire
when it neither crossed the 8px slop nor pinched, so a drag scrolls
natively (pointercancel drops the tap) instead of dropping a clip.

Verified over real touch events: pinch 37->139 ppb at 3.75x with the
focal bar pinned (0px drift), one-finger drag scrolls with momentum,
tap drops a clip, tapping a clip selects it without spawning one.
noodles/96fe1fd:
Builder ask: unify the level meter and the level control without
losing the meter, Ableton-style. One column now does both jobs — an
RMS body (fast attack, slow release) shows perceived level, an
instantaneous peak bar rides above it, a hold tick with a numeric
readout keeps the recent maximum for 1.2 s before letting go, and the
volume handle travels the same column. Dragging is relative anywhere
on the element, so grabbing off-handle never jumps the level. The
column spans the full row the old stacked pair split between them.

Tone.Meter only reports smoothed RMS, so the per-track meters became
waveform analysers: one buffer read yields both RMS and true peak
(audio.meterLevels), and the ballistics live in the mixer's rAF tick.
bits/9634406:
Three bits called "untitled bit" were one bit three times over. Every row
now carries a still of the bit, its cast size, its passes, its length and
when it was last touched. The still is drawn from the recipe through the
same drawStage the stage and the render use, at a moment far enough in
that the puppets have moved — one path to pixels, so a poster can never
show something the film will not. Nothing is stored: a saved poster would
go stale the moment a puppet was recast, and would cost every bit a file.

A bit can be copied, to wreck without losing the original. The copy
shares its assets rather than duplicating eleven megabytes of photo, so
collection now checks whether any living bit still names an asset before
dropping it. That was a latent bug the moment sharing became possible.

A bit file can arrive from another app's share sheet. The manifest
declares the target, and the worker takes the POST before its non-GET
bail-out — a worker that ignores every POST hands the share straight back
to the network and loses the file. It parks the file in a cache, redirects
to the app, and the app collects it once. An imported bit carries a credit
for where it came from, which survives being remixed again, so a chain
stays legible. It is a credit, not a link: nothing is fetched and nothing
merges. Being a line of text straight out of a stranger's file, it is
validated on the way in.

The finished film now opens a sheet with its own still, its length and
its size, and one button that sends it. It used to arrive as a toast and
then live behind the word "share" in a menu, which made the one thing the
whole app is for the hardest thing in it to find.

Six new assertions, including the share round trip through a real service
worker and a copy that keeps its puppets after the original is deleted
and collected. 65/65 checks pass.
